title: Why LeBron James Is the Greatest of All Time
text: Every generation of basketball fans debates who owns the title of Greatest of All Time (GOAT). Pure scorers point to Michael Jordan, dominant big men point to Kareem Abdul-Jabbar or Wilt Chamberlain, and modern shooters point to Stephen Curry. Yet when we examine the complete historical record — 5,160 players in regular-season history and 3,016 players in NBA Playoff history — LeBron James stands completely alone as the most complete basketball player to ever live.

title: Why LeBron James Is the Greatest of All Time
text:
1. Population One: The 3D Points–Rebounds–Assists Space
In basketball history, stars usually specialize: centers rack up points and rebounds, guards rack up points and assists, and wings score. Below are every one of the 414 players in NBA history who scored at least 10,000 career points.

Try it yourself: Drag to rotate the 3D cube and scroll to zoom. Notice how centers cluster along the Rebounds wall, point guards stretch along the Assists floor, and LeBron James floats by himself in the upper-top-right corner.

title: Why LeBron James Is the Greatest of All Time
section: 2. Elite Across Every Skill on the Floor
text:
2. Elite Across Every Skill on the Floor
Out of 5,160 players who have ever logged an NBA minute, LeBron isn’t just #1 in scoring. He ranks near the very top of the entire league’s 78-year history in longevity, passing, perimeter defense, three-point shooting, and rebounding all at once.

title: Longevity & Seasons
text: In NBA history, greatness usually follows a familiar curve: two years of development, an eight-to-ten-year prime, and a steep late-career decline into a role player. LeBron James broke the aging curve. Across 23 NBA seasons, he has averaged 25+ PPG in 20 different seasons — more than any other player has even played at an All-Star level.

title: Longevity & Seasons
section: 1. The Climb to 40,000+: Cumulative Career Scoring Trajectory
text:
1. The Climb to 40,000+: Cumulative Career Scoring Trajectory
Tracking cumulative points by NBA season number reveals two things at once: LeBron matched or beat almost every legend’s pace right out of high school, and then kept climbing steeply long after every peer’s body gave out.

title: Longevity & Seasons
section: 2. Defying Father Time: Scoring Average by Career Season
text:
2. Defying Father Time: Scoring Average by Career Season
Critics sometimes call longevity records “compiler stats.” Look closely at Points Per Game (PPG) in Years 15 through 22+: Kareem, Kobe, Karl Malone, and Tim Duncan all dropped toward 10–19 PPG at the end of their careers. LeBron was still putting up 25 to 30 PPG nearly two decades into his NBA career.

title: Longevity & Seasons
section: 3. Reinventing His Game Across Four Eras
text:
3. Reinventing His Game Across Four Eras
One secret behind LeBron’s longevity is adaptability. As the NBA shifted toward pace-and-space shooting, LeBron transformed from an athletic slasher in his first Cleveland stint into a hyper-efficient post scorer in Miami, an all-court floor general in his return to Cleveland, and an elite high-volume three-point shooter and playmaker with the Lakers.

title: Playoffs & Clutch
text: Regular-season totals tell only half of an NBA career. Championship legacies are forged in the NBA Playoffs, where rotations shrink, defenses game-plan for every tendency, and weak links get exposed. Across all 3,016 players in NBA Playoff history, LeBron James hasn’t merely participated in deep runs — he owns the postseason record book by an almost unthinkable margin.

title: Scoring & Playmaking
text: A common myth about LeBron James is that he is “actually a pass-first player, not a natural scorer” — or conversely, that he broke Kareem Abdul-Jabbar’s scoring record simply by playing a lot of games. Plotting all 5,160 players in NBA history exposes why both myths fall apart: LeBron combines #1 all-time scoring volume with top-4 point-guard playmaking and superior shooting efficiency.

title: Scoring & Playmaking
section: 2. Efficiency Check: Did LeBron Just Shoot More?
text:
2. Efficiency Check: Did LeBron Just Shoot More?
To test efficiency fairly across two-pointers, three-pointers, and free throws, basketball analysts use True Shooting Percentage (TS%):
\[\text{TS\%} = \frac{\text{Points}}{2 \times (\text{FGA} + 0.44 \times \text{FTA})}\]
Below is every 25,000+ point scorer in NBA history, plotting Points Per Game (PPG) against True Shooting Percentage (TS%), with bubble size showing career Assists. LeBron averages 27+ PPG on nearly 59% True Shooting — more efficient than Michael Jordan (56.9%), Kobe Bryant (55.0%), Wilt Chamberlain (54.7%), and Tim Duncan (55.1%) — while simultaneously acting as his team’s primary point guard.

title: About
text:
About the Data
All statistics presented on this website come directly from the official NBA Stats All-Time Leaders Database and NBA Stats Player Career Profiles, accessed via the NBA’s public statistics endpoints and stored locally as clean CSV files for full reproducibility. The dataset covers career regular-season totals and efficiency metrics (including True Shooting Percentage and Effective Field Goal Percentage) for all 5,160 players who have ever appeared in an NBA game, career postseason totals for every NBA playoff participant in league history, and year-by-year season logs comparing LeBron James against fellow all-time greats Michael Jordan, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Kobe Bryant, Stephen Curry, Kevin Durant, and Tim Duncan.

title: GOAT Explorer
text:
Don’t just take our word for it — test the numbers yourself! This exploration hub merges career regular-season totals with career playoff totals for every player in NBA history. We also compute a transparent All-Around Career Impact Score that weights postseason production twice as heavily as regular-season box-score production:
\[\text{Impact Score} = \frac{\text{PTS} + 1.5\,\text{REB} + 2\,\text{AST} + 3\,(\text{STL} + \text{BLK})}{1000} + \frac{\text{Playoff PTS} + 1.5\,\text{Playoff REB} + 2\,\text{Playoff AST}}{500}\]

How to explore: Type any player’s name in the Search box (try Jordan, Jokic, Curry, Wilt, or your favorite role player), click any column header to sort, or use the filter boxes directly underneath each column header to set custom minimum thresholds (for example, filter PTS above 25000 and AST above 5000 to see how few players survive!).
